name: Pootheri Illam (Pootheri Mana)
tagline: Historic Namboothiri illam at Feroke — a Nilambur Kovilakam stronghold and link to Kerala ritual and jyotisha traditions
summary: Pootheri Illam is a historic Namboothiri mana in Feroke, Kozhikode. Once a Nilambur Kovilakam stronghold, it now stands in ruin and connects to Kerala’s ancestral ritual and jyotisha traditions.
description: Pootheri Illam (also called Pootheri Mana) is the ancestral house of a Namboothiri family located in Feroke, Kozhikode. Sources identify it as one of the aristocratic Illams associated with the Nilambur Kovilakam line and show the building in a ruined state today.

The site matters as an example of north Kerala’s Namboothiri tharavad architecture and as a local centre of ritual life: Illams like Pootheri traditionally served as homes for Vedic learning, temple ritual and related practices (including Kerala forms of jyotisha/astrology). Photographs and records show the Pootheri house in decay, and legal records document disputes over its land.

Visitors gain a close-up view of a rarely pictured Feroke heritage site, a sense of how Namboothiri households anchored ritual and social networks, and a tangible connection to the Nilambur–Feroke web of historic alliances. There are no formal visitor facilities — confirm access and opening with local authorities or owners before you go.
highlights: Namboothiri illam in Feroke, listed among well-known Illams of Kerala.
Historic link to Nilambur Kovilakam (built as an aristocratic stronghold in that network).
Visible ruins and photographic record (publicly available images show the decayed manor).
Documented land and possession disputes in Kerala court records — site may be on private or contested land.
Represents north Kerala’s ancestral ritual culture and the wider Namboothiri role in traditional jyotisha.

sections.heading: Background
body: Pootheri Illam is recorded in regional sources as a Namboothiri mana (Illam) located at Feroke in Kozhikode district and as one of the aristocratic houses connected to the Nilambur Kovilakam network. Several reference pages and photographic records describe the building as a former stronghold of Namboothiri lords tied by marriage and alliance to the Nilambur rulers.

Later 20th‑century records and local reports show the Pootheri property falling out of continuous family occupation and the house becoming neglected; public images available online show the structure in ruin. Land and possession disputes over parcels identified as belonging to Pootheri Illam also appear in Kerala court documents.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: View the remaining structure and compound from public access points (photographs in public repositories document its ruined condition). Look for traditional Illam architectural features if visible — timber work, courtyards and compound layout — but note much is dilapidated.

Talk to local residents, municipal heritage officers or historians in Feroke for oral history and context. If you are researching jyotisha or ritual history, use the site as a starting point to locate nearby temples, families and scholars who preserve Namboothiri ritual and astrological knowledge.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: There are no visitor facilities or signposted heritage interpretation at Pootheri Illam. The site appears to be on land with contested ownership in public records, so confirm access before attempting to enter the compound. Treat the site as potentially private and obtain permission from local authorities or owners.

Reach Feroke by regular transport (train or bus to Feroke, then local taxi or auto to the Nallur/Pootheri area). Carry a local map, ask the Feroke municipality or a local guide for the exact location, and plan modest time onsite — the main visit is an exterior observation and local inquiry.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November–February (post‑monsoon, pleasant); avoid heavy monsoon months.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Travel to Feroke (served by Feroke railway station and Kozhikode–Feroke buses). From Feroke take a local taxi/auto to the Pootheri / Nallur area; confirm exact location and access with locals or Feroke municipality before visiting.
etiquette: Confirm access — court records show land disputes and parts of the property may be private.
Respect local privacy and ritual practice; ask permission before entering or photographing interiors and family compounds.
Carry a local map and ask Feroke municipal office or neighbourhood residents for directions — the site is not a formal tourist attraction.
Avoid drones or intrusive photography without written permission from landowners/authorities.
